name: Introduction and overview — Gearing-class Destroyer — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Gearing-class Destroyer
description: Introduction and overview of the Gearing-class Destroyer: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Gearing class was the ultimate WWII U.S. destroyer: 98 built with a lengthened hull for more fuel and range. Many received FRAM modernizations in the 1960s for Cold War anti-submarine duty. Gearings served the U.S. Navy into the 1980s and allied navies far longer. Baseline facts: U.S. destroyer class; 98 built; lengthened Fletcher hull; FRAM modernizations..
how_it_works: Buoyancy supports the hull; propellers driven by diesel, turbine, or nuclear plant provide thrust; rudders and thrusters steer; stability comes from hull form and ballast.
